value: eyes reduced to small, horn-like eyestalk rudiments set widely apart on a common eyeplate
eye: eyestalk rudiments on an eyeplate, adult male holotype
method: taxonomic description of the holotype, with material from three deep-sea stations
conditions: Description of the adult male holotype (body length 6.6 mm, ZMH 58250, DIVA-1 station 350, Angola Basin, 5433 m, 29 Jul. 2000); nine paratypes (adult and immature males and females, 3.4 to 8.0 mm) from stations 344, 348 and 350 are listed, and the paper does not say how many were checked for the eyes. The sentence before it in the Description reads 'Eyes without visual elements.' The sentence after it says the eyeplate is dorsally covered by the rostral plate, so only part of the rudiments projects behind the rostrum in dorsal view. The Discussion reads the horns and lappets as remnants of convergent eye reduction in dark, deep waters, and the word 'probably' hedges the homology with the ocular symphysis.

value: male eyes bare and holoptic (meeting on the midline), the length of eye contiguity about equal to the length of the ocellar triangle
eye: compound eyes, males
method: taxonomic description of pinned male specimens
conditions: Male description from the holotype (male, Entebbe, Uganda, 21.8.11, C.C. Gowdey, NHMUK) and 28 male paratypes from Uganda localities (Entebbe, Lake Albert, Mbarara, Mabamba Swamps; 1906 to 2018); no females are known, so the female eye state is unrecorded. The Differential diagnosis also calls the male holoptic. The congener M. caffer is described in the same paper with males 'slightly dichoptic, distance between eyes approx. the width of ocellus'. The M. arcuatus account has no Variation section (the paper's Variation text is under M. caffer).

value: 12 ommatidia in the compound eye of the gyne (the sentence uses the singular 'compound eye' and does not say how many gynes were counted)
eye: compound eye, gyne (the paper's ergatogyne, a reproductive female 'completely lacking alar sclerites')
method: morphological description of preserved specimens (some with micro-CT in the paper)
conditions: Material is from Vietnam: Cuc Phuong NP, Ninh Binh (4 workers, 1 gyne CASENT0842884, 30 larvae, 8 Aug 2022) and Tay Yen Tu Nature Reserve, Bac Giang (2003: 2 males, 1 worker, 1 gyne; 2004: 1 worker); the species is not newly described here and no type is designated. The text never describes worker eyes directly; the gyne entry says 'As for worker, but with compound eye', which implies workers lack compound eyes. Two gynes are in the material and the measurement sample is n = 2; the figure shows the single gyne CASENT0842884. The paper does not say whether 12 is per eye or for both, and gives no count for the male eyes. The eye is described as small (REL = 10) against 'large (REL = 53-57)' in the male; the gyne measurements (n = 2) give 'REL = 8–10', so the two gynes differ in relative eye length, and the paper does not say which gyne gave the 12-ommatidia count. The Remarks call this female an ergatogyne: 'alar sclerites are completely lacking in the ergatogyne of P. gengma', against 'Most Protanilla gynes are alate'. The Remarks do not discuss eyes.

value: male compound eyes large (REL 53 to 57) and oval, all margins weakly convex
eye: compound eyes, males
method: morphological description of preserved specimens
conditions: Material is from Vietnam: Cuc Phuong NP, Ninh Binh (4 workers, 1 gyne CASENT0842884, 30 larvae, 8 Aug 2022) and Tay Yen Tu Nature Reserve, Bac Giang (2003: 2 males, 1 worker, 1 gyne; 2004: 1 worker); the species is not newly described here and no type is designated. The text never describes worker eyes directly; the gyne entry says 'As for worker, but with compound eye', which implies workers lack compound eyes. Two males are in the material and the male measurement sample is n = 2 (REL 53 to 57). The male description also says 'Ocellar tubercle absent.' (the sentence before the eye sentence is 'Occipital carina present only dorsally.'). The gyne eye is small (REL = 10 in the description, 8–10 in the measurements of n = 2) with 12 ommatidia; the paper calls this female an ergatogyne completely lacking alar sclerites.
